Prepare covariate balance data for plotting

Source: R/covariate-balance.R
hv_balance.Rd

Validates and orders a long-format standardized-mean-difference data frame for a covariate balance plot, and returns an hv_balance object. Call plot.hv_balance on the result to obtain a bare ggplot2 object that you can decorate with color, shape, axis scales, and theme_hv_manuscript.

Usage

hv_balance(
  data,
  variable_col = "variable",
  group_col = "group",
  std_diff_col = "std_diff",
  var_levels = NULL,
  threshold = 10,
  stat_col = NULL,
  pair_col = NULL,
  stats = "smd",
  vr_threshold = c(0.5, 2),
  ks_threshold = NULL,
  group_labels = c("Before", "After")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format with one row per covariate \(\times\) group combination. Wide-format data must be reshaped first (e.g. with tidyr::pivot_longer()). It may instead be a cobalt::bal.tab() result (built with un = TRUE to draw the Before group), an hvtiRpropensity ps_* object, or a list of those, one per imputation; see Details.

variable_col

Name of the column containing covariate labels. Default "variable".

group_col

Name of the column identifying the comparison group (e.g. "Before match" / "After match"). Default "group".

std_diff_col

Name of the numeric column holding standardized mean difference values. Default "std_diff".

var_levels

Character vector controlling the display order of covariates on the y-axis. The first element appears at the bottom. Defaults to the order of first appearance in data[[variable_col]].

threshold

Numeric; absolute SMD value at which dotted reference lines are drawn (\(\pm\)threshold). Default 10.

stat_col

Optional name of a column holding the statistic each row reports: "smd", "variance_ratio" or "ks". When NULL (default) every row is treated as "smd".

pair_col

Optional name of a column identifying the comparison (e.g. "B vs. A") when more than two groups were compared. Default NULL (a single comparison).

stats

Character vector of statistics to keep, in panel order; any of "smd", "variance_ratio", "ks". Default "smd". An error is raised if a requested statistic has no rows.

vr_threshold

One or two positive numbers; reference lines for the variance-ratio panel. Default c(0.5, 2).

ks_threshold

NULL (no line, default) or a single number in \([0,1]\); reference line for the KS panel.

group_labels

Length-2 character vector naming the before and after groups. Default c("Before", "After").

Value

An object of class c("hv_balance", "hv_data"): a list with three elements:

$data

The input data frame with a cb_index column added for y-axis positioning, a stat factor (levels = stats) and a pair column (NA when there are no comparisons, otherwise a factor in order of first appearance). If data already has its own stat or pair column it is left untouched and these values go in .cb_stat / .cb_pair.

$meta

Named list: variable_col, group_col, std_diff_col, var_levels, threshold, n_vars, n_groups, stats, pairs, stat_var and pair_var (the names of the columns holding the statistic and the comparison), n_imputations, vr_threshold, ks_threshold, suggested_height.

$tables

Empty list (no accessory tables).

Details

Instead of a long data frame, data may be a cobalt::bal.tab() result, a multi-category bal.tab (one facet row per pair), an hvtiRpropensity ps_match() / ps_weight() object, or a list of any one of those, one per imputation. In those cases the SMD is multiplied by 100 and the *_col arguments are ignored.

A bal.tab() result must be built with binary = "std" and continuous = "std" (the default), so every difference is standardized, and with un = TRUE to draw the Before group: cobalt leaves the unadjusted columns empty otherwise, and hv_balance() then says so in a message and draws the After group only. Ask for the variance ratio and KS statistic with stats = c("m", "v", "ks"); the variance ratio is undefined for binary covariates, so those rows are left out of its panel. A distance or prop.score row (Type "Distance") is drawn as a covariate row, as in cobalt::love.plot(). ps_* objects carry standardized differences only.

A list is pooled across imputations: SMD and KS statistic are averaged, the variance ratio takes the geometric mean, and an NA in any imputation makes the pooled value NA (counted in $meta$n_missing). Every imputation must have the same rows, with one allowance: a covariate cobalt types as binary in some imputations (because it takes two values there) has no variance ratio in those, so its pooled variance ratio is NA.

See also

Worked recipe with rendered output: https://ehrlinger.github.io/hvtiGraphics/balance.html.

plot.hv_balance, sample_covariate_balance_data

Examples

library(ggplot2)
dta <- sample_covariate_balance_data()

# 1. Build data object
cb <- hv_balance(dta)
cb  # prints variable count, group count, threshold
#> <hv_balance>
#>   Variables   : 12
#>   Groups      : 2 (Before match, After match)
#>   Value col   : std_diff
#>   Threshold   : ±10
#>   Stats       : smd
#>   Height      : 3.5 in at 12 pt (see hv_balance_height())

# 2. Bare plot -- undecorated ggplot returned by plot.hv_balance
p <- plot(cb)

# 3. Decorate: color/shape palettes, x-axis range, labels, theme
p +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Before match" = "red4", "After match" = "blue3"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Before match" = 17L, "After match" = 15L),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-45, 35), breaks = seq(-40, 30, 10)) +
  labs(x = "Standardized difference (%)", y = "") +
  theme_hv_poster()
#> Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_point()`).


# 4. From a cobalt::bal.tab() result: SMD, variance ratio and KS panels
if (requireNamespace("cobalt", quietly = TRUE)) {
  lal <- cobalt::lalonde
  ps  <- fitted(glm(treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
                    data = lal, family = binomial()))
  bt <- cobalt::bal.tab(
    treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
    data = lal, weights = ifelse(lal$treat == 1, 1 / ps, 1 / (1 - ps)),
    binary = "std", s.d.denom = "pooled", stats = c("m", "v", "ks"), un = TRUE
  )
  plot(hv_balance(bt, stats = c("smd", "variance_ratio", "ks")))
}
